description: Curated collection of seminal open-access scientific papers in deep learning, Transformers, Knowledge Graphs, and RAG for real-world pilot evaluation.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.abstract: Large pre-trained language models have been shown to store factual knowledge in their parameters, and achieve state-of-the-art results when fine-tuned on downstream NLP tasks. However, their ability to access and precisely manipulate knowledge is still limited. In this work, we explore retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models, which combine pre-trained parametric memory with non-parametric neural retrieval.

papers.title: Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of embedding entities and relationships of multi-relational data into low-dimensional vector spaces. Our goal is to propose a canonical model which is easy to train, offers a small number of parameters and can scale up to very large databases. We introduce TransE, an energy-based model for learning low-dimensional embeddings of knowledge graphs.

papers.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Language model pre-training has been shown to capture a substantial amount of world knowledge, crucial for NLP tasks such as question answering. However, this knowledge is stored implicitly in the parameters of a neural network. We present REALM, which augments language models with a learned neural knowledge retriever.

papers.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
papers.abstract: We introduce LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters. We train our models on trillions of tokens, and show that it is possible to train state-of-the-art models using publicly available datasets exclusively, without resorting to proprietary and inaccessible datasets.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.abstract: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions.
